newsitem.title: UK: CE defends use of Northern valuation.
newsitem.headline: CE defends use of Northern valuation.

text.p: U.S. group CalEnergy believes its use of a valuation of bid target Northern Electric by Northern's stockbrokers BZW on a "base case" scenario at 484 pence per share was "entirely legitimate," a spokesman said.
BZW had earlier said it took issue with the use of the valuation, which it said was one of a number calculated for illustrative purposes.

It said CalEnergy, which is bidding 630 pence per share for Northern through its 70 percent-owned unit CE Electric, had "quoted selectively...from a BZW presentation to institutional clients which ran a number of models."

BZW added that on the same "base case" valuation, East Midlands Electricty would be 459 pence per share. As Dominion Resources agreed a bid for East Midlands last week at 46 percent above this price, BZW observed, the same uplift would price Northern at 706 pence.
"It is an extreme exercise in sophistry trying to get to 700 pence on this basis," the CalEnergy spokesman said.
Northern has claimed CalEnergy suggested a price of 700 pence before it launched its bid, but CalEnergy has consistently denied that.

CalEnergy already owns just under 30 percent of Northern and the regional electricity company's shares were trading under the bid level at 596-1/2 pence by 1600 GMT as concerns the bid might be blocked by the UK government overhang the market.
